notes: Changing a port's role no longer deletes your configuration without asking. Dropping a port's WAN role deletes every egress on that port, and ON DELETE CASCADE takes the PPPoE accounts and the NAT port-forwards with them -- measured on a copy of a live router's database, turning its two pppoe_wan ports into lan_phone took egress 2 -> 0, pppoe_accounts 2 -> 0 and nat_ports 14 -> 0 from a single click, with no warning. That, not the restore, is what emptied a configuration and made restoring a backup look like it had never worked: restore, set the port back to LAN, and it is destroyed again. Saving a role now answers 409 with the exact counts unless the request confirms them, and the role selector shows them in a red dialog first. Only losses that were actually configured count, so dhcp_wan -> pppoe_wan stays a one-click change. Restore itself had a separate silent hole: with no destination path to write to it reported success having written nothing, and the handler reboots as soon as restore returns OK -- so the router came back on the very configuration you were replacing, after being told the restore worked. It now fails instead. The release gate runs 34 tests, up from 26.
